title: Joining Bill Matthews' band after Paul Barbarin
summary: He took the Matthews job about five years earlier, playing mostly jump numbers and the Saints.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When did you join Bill Matthews? How long has that been now?
Well, a rough guess, I think it's about five years.
Because I was with Paul Barberin.

At the time, I was with Paul Barberin, and, well, they asked me, they offered me the job. I threw it down the first time. You could have it. Well, the next time, I came from Paul Barberin and do nothing much, so I just accepted it. And I've been with them ever since.

How do you like that kind of work, Alba? Well, it's all right. I mean, what do you think of the kind of music? I mean, I notice you hardly ever play blues. It's all pretty well, I must say, jump numbers. Yes. Do you find that kind of hard work?
Well, it is kind of hard, because it would be a little easier if you play a couple of fast ones and a slow one.

They make you play the saints almost every set, I guess. Almost every set. You do that marching around the place. I guess the tourists like it all right. Were there some other bands in there, any other notes that you had there that you wanted to go over? We're just about through with that tape here. We don't want to bother you so much about every little detail, but I thought if there were some other bands you might have left out, any other notes on the paper that you wanted to mention before we...
